verdict.rationale: Supermemory's own docs describe a knowledge graph built from memories, with graph traversal at retrieval time and a related-memories option shown on an entity-style query ("where does Alex work?"). However, the graph is described as facts linked to other facts, not as explicit entities and typed relationships, and nothing documents multi-hop query answering. All evidence is vendor docs. Missing for 10: an explicit entity/relationship schema or extraction, documented multi-hop traversal behaviour, entity-centric query APIs beyond the relatedMemories flag, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can store memories as a knowledge graph of entities and relationships so multi-hop and entity-centric questions are answerable

citations.quote: Supermemory builds a living knowledge graph of facts on top of other facts — not a static folder of embeddings
Retrieve three ways — document search (RAG), memory graph traversal, and user profile
const results = await client.search({ q: "where does Alex work?", containerTag: "user_123", include: { relatedMemories: true }, });
Local graph engine, local embeddings, local LLM.
